# C2 — Unnecessary Call Overhead

*Level 1 card. 3 root causes. Open the level-2 card before accepting any of them.*

Energy waste from extra layers of function calls, method delegation, or dynamic dispatch that add overhead without proportional benefit. This includes trivial wrapper methods that only forward to another function (unnecessary delegation), instance methods that never access self and could be static (missing static declaration), and performance-critical code paths split into too many tiny functions whose combined call overhead exceeds the useful work (excessive modularization). In Python, each function call creates a frame object, pushes arguments onto the call stack, and manages return values, making call overhead a significant factor in hot paths.

## Root causes in this category

| ID | Name | The repair | Measurable? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C2.S1** | Unnecessary Method Delegation | call the delegate directly from the hot call site | yes, scales with call count |
| **C2.S2** | Missing Static Declaration | mark it `@staticmethod` so no bound method object is built per call | yes, scales with call count |
| **C2.S3** | Excessive Modularization in Hot Path | merge the thin layers into one function on the hot path | yes, scales with input |

Card paths: `reference/root-causes/C2.S1.md`, `reference/root-causes/C2.S2.md`, `reference/root-causes/C2.S3.md`

## Telling this category from its neighbours

These come up often enough to check before you commit:

- **C2.S3 vs C3.S3 Inefficient Per-Iteration Setup** — C2.S3 is about the *number of call layers* per iteration.  C3.S3 is about *work that could have happened once* before the loop.  If the repair is "hoist it", that is C3.S3, not this.

## If nothing here fits

Say so and move on. Reporting a weak match from an already-open category is the most common way this analysis goes wrong: the category is open because a static signal pointed at it, not because a smell is there.
